clue.text: Corps of non-British origin? Germanic, conceivably

definitions.text: Corps of non-British origin? Germanic, conceivably

parts.words: Corps of non-British origin? Germanic, conceivably
parts.note: a Germanic group would count as one from a British viewpoint, while the medical sense is an object lodged where it should not be

explanation.surface: A question about whether a military corps from abroad might be German.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Corps' as a body and 'non-British origin' as from abroad; a German contingent would qualify.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally describes a group from another country, as well as a stray object inside the human frame.

clue.text: Put on wrong feeding

indicators.note: something done wrong is mixed up, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone has been given the wrong food or fitted the wrong feeding tube.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges FEEDING. 'Put on' is used as in putting on an act.
explanation.definitionFit: To put on an emotion is to pretend it, to fake it.

clue.text: Skilled operator from the air-raid post, oddly enough

indicators.note: things arranged oddly are out of their usual order, telling us to shuffle the fourteen letters of the phrase before

explanation.surface: A trained wartime worker emerges from a civil defence shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly enough' rearranges THE AIR-RAID POST; an air-raid post was a Second World War civil defence station.
explanation.definitionFit: A clinician trained to operate radiation equipment for cancer treatment is a skilled operator of machines.

clue.text: Only one transport for him

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
a van is a vehicle, a means of transport

explanation.surface: A single vehicle reserved for one particular man.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is just 'him': a man's name, here the Russian form of John.
explanation.definitionFit: A male first name stands for a particular man, referred to by a pronoun.

clue.text: Wherein work is not all child's play

definitions.text: Wherein work is not all child's play

parts.words: Wherein work is not all child's play
parts.note: a place for small children where staff work hard; also a garden where plants are raised, and play is the children's business

explanation.surface: A remark that looking after toddlers is harder than it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: A room or school for infants is where children play but the carers have real work to do.

clue.text: See 1
Bit more than 21 goes to make this initiation

indicators.note: the letters go into making something new, so they are rearranged

parts.note: 21 across is AMPS, so the number stands for those letters

explanation.surface: Something slightly more than a reference number is needed for a rite of passage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes to make' rearranges BIT plus AMPS (the answer to 21 across).
explanation.definitionFit: A christening is the Christian rite of admission into the Church, an initiation ceremony.

clue.text: Computers store it, thanks to an American lawman

indicators.note: thanks is added to the lawman, so it comes after

parts.note: DA is a District Attorney, an American prosecutor
ta is informal British for thank you

explanation.surface: Gratitude expressed towards a US law officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' here means added on, so the thanks follows the lawman; DA is a common US abbreviation solvers abroad may not know as a prosecutor's title.
explanation.definitionFit: Information held in digital form is what computer memories hold.

clue.text: Improvises with a smoked dish

indicators.note: to dish something is to ruin it, so the letters are spoiled into a new order

explanation.surface: A cook throws together a meal using a smoked dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dish' (as in to wreck) rearranges A SMOKED.
explanation.definitionFit: To manage with what is available is to improvise.

clue.text: Never despair of Latin

parts.note: the clue gives the English meaning and says the phrase wanted is the Latin version of it

explanation.surface: An instruction not to give up on studying Latin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of Latin' looks like the subject of the despair, but it asks for the Latin motto meaning 'never despair'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin tag is a translation of the English instruction not to lose hope.

clue.text: I drink a nice port blended for illusory effect

indicators.note: a blend mixes ingredients, so the letters of the phrase before are mixed up

explanation.surface: A drinker mixes a pleasant port to get a dreamy feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blended' rearranges I DRINK A NICE PORT.
explanation.definitionFit: The fabled conjuring feat of climbing a rope into the air is a famous illusion.

clue.text: A time to reflect

indicators.note: the word mirrors itself, reading the same in either direction

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A suggestion that some moment is good for quiet thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to reflect' says the answer reads the same backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Midday is a particular hour of the day.

clue.text: Mountain in a West African republic

parts.note: ben is Scottish for a mountain, as in Ben Nevis

explanation.surface: A peak located in some African state.
explanation.definitionFit: The country is a republic on the Gulf of Guinea in West Africa.

clue.text: Compositions partly good, especially in rhyme

indicators.note: only part of the words is used, so the answer lies inside them

explanation.surface: Pieces of writing that are fairly good, particularly the rhyming ones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partly' finds the answer inside gOOD ESpecially; 'in rhyme' adds colour, since these poems usually rhyme.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyric poems are literary compositions.

clue.text: Type of contract that could trap the unwary

definitions.text: Type of contract that could trap the unwary

parts.words: Type of contract that could trap the unwary
parts.note: the tiny lettering in a contract hides conditions careless readers miss

explanation.surface: A warning about a kind of agreement that catches out careless people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Type' looks like 'kind', but it means printed characters.
explanation.definitionFit: The tiny-lettered terms of an agreement often hide unwelcome conditions.

clue.text: See 13
Once a country dwelling built in 24 hours, now 11

indicators.note: the dwelling is constructed inside the period of time

parts.note: a day lasts 24 hours
a home is a dwelling

explanation.surface: A house put up within a single day.
explanation.walkthrough: '24' is not a reference to 24 down here, just a number. 'now 11' adds that the country is today the answer to 11 across, the republic it was renamed in 1975.
explanation.definitionFit: This West African state took a new name in 1975, so it is a former nation.

clue.text: Lively dance displaying social conventions to a little firm

indicators.note: the firm is added to the conventions, so it follows them

parts.note: mores are the customs and conventions of a society
Co is the short form of company, a firm

explanation.surface: Showing good manners to a small business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' means added on, so the abbreviated firm follows the conventions; 'displaying' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A Moorish dance, related to the morris, is a lively traditional step.

clue.text: Creature found by a stream in United Indian Territory

indicators.note: the stream is placed inside the name of the territory

parts.note: Goa was once part of a Union Territory of India
a rill is a small stream

explanation.surface: An animal spotted by a brook in part of India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'United' points to India's Union Territories, of which Goa was part until 1987; 'found by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The great ape is an animal.

clue.text: Nobleman with magnificent energy, note

parts.note: grand means splendid, magnificent
E is the symbol for energy in physics
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: An aristocrat with splendid vigour and a written note.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spanish or Portuguese high-ranking aristocrat is a nobleman.

clue.text: Where Granny Smith gets by in Cumbria

definitions.text: Where Granny Smith gets by in Cumbria

parts.note: a Granny Smith is a variety of apple

explanation.surface: An old woman named Smith manages to scrape by in the north of England.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines a place, while 'Granny Smith gets by' gives APPLE + BY. Cumbria is a county in northwest England; the town is famous for its horse fair.
explanation.definitionFit: The market town is in Cumbria, where the variety meets the word by.

clue.text: Ray down the shaft

parts.note: a shaft can be a beam of light, so a ray coming down in it from the sky; the surface suggests a man named Ray in a mine

explanation.surface: A man called Ray is down the mine shaft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ray' looks like a man's name, but it is a beam of light, and a shaft of light is the same thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A beam of sunshine falls in a shaft of light from the sky.

clue.text: Free from transgressions the French embody

annotationWithheld.why: Free from transgressions the French embody (7): the only parse puts LES (the French) inside SINS (transgressions), with 'transgressions' also needed in the definition 'Free from transgressions', so one word does two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Free from transgressions the French embody

clue.text: The Scotsman looked to be rich

parts.note: mon is the Scots form of man
to eye something is to look at it

explanation.surface: A Scot appeared to be wealthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Scotsman' gives MON, how a man is addressed in Scots dialect.
explanation.definitionFit: Having plenty of cash means being wealthy.

clue.text: In which a parliamentarian's strength is currently measured?

definitions.text: In which a parliamentarian's strength is currently measured?

parts.note: an MP is a Member of Parliament, and the possessive adds S

explanation.surface: A question about how a politician's power is now judged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'currently' means in terms of electric current: current strength is measured in these units. A + MP'S also builds the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Electric current is measured in units named after Ampère.

clue.text: What Rumpelstiltskin did with malicious intent

definitions.text: What Rumpelstiltskin did with malicious intent

parts.words: What Rumpelstiltskin did with malicious intent
parts.note: the fairy-tale imp turned straw into gold on a spinning wheel to trap the miller's daughter; the phrase also means telling a tall story

explanation.surface: An account of the sinister activity of a fairy-tale goblin.
explanation.walkthrough: Rumpelstiltskin spun straw into gold in exchange for a firstborn child; the idiom also means telling a tall story.
explanation.definitionFit: The imp worked a spinning wheel, and the idiom also means told an invented story.

clue.text: See 22
Be positive albeit negative one hears

indicators.note: says that the word is spoken and heard, not seen written

parts.note: no is a negative answer

explanation.surface: An upbeat person sounding a pessimistic note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one hears' says NO sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To be certain of something is to be sure, positive.

clue.text: Volcano before erupting

indicators.note: a volcano erupting throws things about, so the letters of the synonym are scattered

parts.note: ante is Latin for before, as in ante meridiem

explanation.surface: A volcano just prior to its eruption.
explanation.walkthrough: 'erupting' rearranges ANTE, from 'before'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sicilian mountain is an active volcano.

clue.text: How unbiased mediators should settle arguments

definitions.text: How unbiased mediators should settle arguments

parts.words: How unbiased mediators should settle arguments
parts.note: describes the impartial manner of a neutral judge, without personal stake

explanation.surface: Advice on the right way for neutral go-betweens to resolve disputes.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting impartially, without personal gain, is the right manner for a neutral arbitrator.

clue.text: Move unsteadily with rem recurring tropical disease

indicators.note: something recurring comes back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: yaws is a tropical skin infection

explanation.surface: Wobbling while suffering a returning fever from the tropics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recurring' turns YAWS round.
explanation.definitionFit: To rock or totter is to move unsteadily.

clue.text: Made an impact at the card table

explanation.surface: Someone who made a big impression playing cards.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, a slam is winning all or all but one of the tricks; to be slammed at the table is to have that happen.
explanation.definitionFit: Struck hard means made an impact; at bridge, winning every trick is a grand slam.
